# YM28: 四宜书屋 Siyi Shuwu, "The Library of the Four Delights"

Malone calls it Ssu I Shu Wu.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM28` · Page: `/scenes/#YM28` · Row: `research/buildings/YM28-siyi-shuwu/`

## What it was

四宜书屋 Siyi Shuwu, east of 西峰秀色 past two pairs of boathouses, on the north bank: the five-bay 四宜书屋, main hall of 安澜园 Anlan Yuan; south-east 葄经馆, south 采芳洲, behind it 飞睇亭, north-east 绿帷舫, south-west 无边风月之阁, further south-west 涵秋堂, north 烟月清真楼, west of that 远秀山房, and across a curved bridge north 染霞楼 (S05 j82:8a-b; E1815). The plaque 四宜书屋 is Yongzheng's; Qianlong reshaped the site after the garden of the Chen family at Haining, whose name 安澜 he had granted in 1762 (壬午), and explained it as a wish for safe sea walls, Yellow River and Grand Canal (E1814, S05 安澜园记; E1819, S02). S361 says it was first called 春宇舒和 (E1820). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **changed** Remodelled after Haining 隅园 (安澜园) c. 1762-64 [j82:9a; poems 1764]; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S01).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "春宜花夏宜風秋宜月冬宜雪居處之適也" (S05 j82:8b): spring suits flowers, summer wind, autumn the moon, winter snow; a house fit for all four seasons, among a thousand trees, with blue peaks in the distance.

### How later sources differ

The 1744 leaf shows the Yongzheng-era 四宜书屋. Qianlong's essay says that twenty years after the album the buildings needed repair, and he used the repair to rearrange the halls round 四宜书屋 'so that they match the Chen garden turn for turn' (就四宜書屋左右前後畧經位置即與陳園曲折如一無二也, E1814, S05 j82:9a); the ten poems on 安澜园 are dated 1764 (乾隆二十九年, E1809, S05 j82:10a-12a). So the 1860 model follows S05 1774 and S01, not the leaf. The Yongzheng plaque stayed (皇考御額在焉, E1809).
